source_text: μου εὐώδους διακοσίους πεντήκοντα, καὶ ἴρεως πεντακοσίους σίκλους τοῦ ἁγίου, καὶ ἔλαιον ἐξ ἐλαιῶν ἔσται, καὶ ποιήσεις αὐτὸ ἔλαιον χρίσμα ἅγιον μύρον μυρεψικὸν τέχνῃ μυρεψοῦ. Ἔλαιον χρίσμα ἅγιον ἔσται. Καὶ χρίσεις ἐξ αὐτοῦ τὴν σκηνὴν τοῦ μαρτυρίου, καὶ τὴν κιβωτὸν τῆς σκηνῆς τοῦ μαρτυρίου καὶ πάντα τὰ σκεύη αὐτῆς, καὶ τὴν λυχνίαν καὶ πάντα τὰ σκεύη αὐτῆς, καὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον τοῦ θυμιάματος, καὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον τῶν ὁλοκαυτωμάτων, καὶ πάντα αὐτοῦ τὰ σκεύη, καὶ τὴν τράπεζαν καὶ πάντα τὰ σκεύη αὐτῆς, καὶ τὸν λουτῆρα, καὶ τὴν βάσιν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἁγιάσεις αὐτά· καὶ ἔσται Ἅγια τῶν ἀγίων. Πᾶς ὁ ἁπτόμενος αὐτῶν, ἁγιασθήσεται. Καὶ Ἀαρὼν καὶ τοὺς υἱοὺς αὐτοῦ χρίσεις, καὶ ἁγιάσεις αὐτοὺς ἱερατεύειν μοι. Καὶ τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραὴλ λαλήσεις, λέγων· Ἔλαιον ἄλειμμα χρίσεως ἅγιον ἔσται τοῦτο ὑμῖν εἰς τὰς γενεὰς ὑμῶν· ἐπὶ σάρκα ἀνθρώπου οὐ χρισθήσεται, καὶ κατὰ τὴν σύνθεσιν ταύτην οὐ ποιήσετε ὑμῖν ἑαυτοῖς ὡσαύτως. Ἅγιόν ἐστι, καὶ ἁγίασμα ἔσται ὑμῖν. Ὃς ἂν ποιήσῃ ὡσαύτως, καὶ ὃς ἂν δῷ ἀπ' αὐτοῦ ἀλλογενεῖ, ἐξολοθρευθήσεται ἐκ τοῦ λαοῦ αὐτοῦ.» Ποιότητος μὲν οὖνπερ, καὶ μὴν καὶ συνθήκης, ἀνισότητός τε αὖ, τῆς εἰς ὁλκὴν δὴ, λέγω, τῶν ὠνομασμένων εἰδῶν, οὐδὲν ἂν ἔχοιμι φράσαι· φίλη γὰρ ἡ ἀλήθεια τοῖς εὖ φρονεῖν εἰωθόσιν. Ἔλαιον δὲ μύροις ἀνακραθὲν, κατασημήνειεν ἂν, ὥσπερ οὖν ἐγᾦμαι, τὸν ἐν Χριστῷ διὰ Πνεύματος ἁγιασμὸν τοῖς ἠλεημένοις χορηγούμενον. Κατά γε τὸ, «Ἐλίπανας ἐν ἐλαίῳ τὴν κεφαλήν μου.» Καταχρίεται δὲ ἡ σκηνὴ, καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ, μετάσχοι γὰρ ἂν ἁγιασμοῦ καὶ τόπος διὰ τοῦ ἐνοικοῦντος ἐν αὐτῷ. Ἁγιάζεται δὲ καὶ τὰ σκεύη, κατά γε τὸν αὐτοῖς πρέποντα τρόπον, ὅτι ταῖς Θεοῦ λειτουργίαις χρήσιμα, καὶ ὁ ἁπτόμενος αὐτῶν ἁγιασθήσεται. Ἀνέπαφα δὴ οὖν τοῖς ἔτι βεβήλοις τὰ ἅγιά τε καὶ ἱερά· «Τίς γὰρ κοινωνία φωτὶ πρὸς σκότος;» κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον. Ἀποφάσκει δὲ παντελῶς τὸ δεῖν ἑαυτοῖς τὴν ὁμοίαν ἐλαίου ποιεῖσθαι κατασκευήν. Ἴδιον γὰρ μόνου τὸ ἁγιάζειν ἐστὶ τοῦ Θεοῦ, καὶ ὡς ἐξαίρετον ἀληθῶς ἀνακείσεται τὸ χρῆμα αὐτῷ, γενητῇ δὲ καὶ πεποιημένῃ φύσει τὸ ἁγιάζειν ἑτέρους δύνασθαι, πῶς ἂν ἔχοι ποτέ; Πλουτεῖ γὰρ μόλις ἐκ μετοχῆς τῆς ἄνωθεν τὸν ἁγιασμόν. Πρέποι δ' ἂν αὐτῇ διὰ τῆς τῶν ἁγίων ἐπιβοᾶσθαι φωνῆς. «Τί γὰρ ἔχεις ὃ οὐκ ἔλαβες;» Καὶ γὰρ Ἰωάννης φησὶ περὶ τοῦ Μονογενοῦς, ὅτι «Ἐκ τοῦ πληρώματος αὐτοῦ ἡμεῖς πάντες ἐλάβομεν.» Καὶ, «Οὐκ ἐκ μέτρου δίδωσι τὸ Πνεῦμα,» πηγὴ δὲ μᾶλλον ὑπάρχων αὐτὸς ἁγιασμοῦ, ἐπιμετρεῖ τοῖς ἀξίοις τὸ Πνεῦμα, καὶ τὴν λογικὴν ἁγιάζει κτίσιν· «Ἐπὶ σάρκα δὲ ἀνθρώπου, φησὶν, οὐ χρισθήσεται,» καίτοι προστεταχὼς καταχρίεσθαι δεῖν ἀπ' αὐτοῦ, τόν τε Ἀαρὼν καὶ τοὺς συνιερατεύοντας. Οὐκοῦν ὑπὲρ ἀνθρώπινον τὸ γένος ἤδη τὸ ἱερὸν, ἅτε δὴ καὶ Χριστοῦ μέτοχον τοῦ ὑπὲρ τὴν κτίσιν. Τοιγάρτοι καὶ πρὸς τὸ ὑπὲρ φύσιν ἡμᾶς ἀνακομίζων ἀξίωμα, καὶ οἱονεὶ τῶν ἐπιγείων ἀποτεμὼν, τοῖς ἄνω προσνέμει· «Πατέρα» γὰρ, φησὶ,
pass_a_gloss: [cont. quotation] '[kala]mou euōdous 250, and iris (iris) 500 sikloi tou hagiou, and elaion ex elaiōn estai; make it elaion chrisma hagion, myron myrepsikon (perfumer's ointment) technē myrepsou; elaion chrisma hagion estai. chriseis (anoint) with it the skēnē tou martyriou, the kibōtos and all its skeuē, the lychnia and its skeuē, the thysiastērion tou thymiamatos, the thysiastērion tōn holokautōmatōn and its skeuē, the trapeza and its skeuē, the loutēr and its basis; hagiaseis them; they shall be Hagia tōn hagiōn; pas ho haptomenos hagiasthēsetai. Aaron and his sons chriseis, hagiaseis to hierateuein for me. To the sons of Israel: elaion aleimma chriseōs hagion for your geneai; epi sarka anthrōpou ou christhēsetai; kata tēn synthesin tautēn you shall not make hōsautōs for yourselves; hagion, hagiasma to you. Whoever makes hōsautōs and gives of it to an allogenēs exolothreuthēsetai from his laos.' Of the poiotēs, synthesis/synthēkē, and anisotēs eis holkēn (inequality of weight) of the eidē named, ouden an echoimi phrasai; philē the alētheia to those wont eu phronein. Elaion myrois anakrathen (blended) would katasēmēneien the hagiasmos en Christō dia Pneumatos chorēgoumenos to the ēleēmenoi; as 'elipanas (you anointed richly) en elaiō my head.' The skēnē katachrietai and all in it; a topos also metaschoi hagiasmou through the one enoikōn in it. The skeuē hagiazetai kata ton preponta tropon, as chrēsima for God's leitourgiai; ho haptomenos hagiasthēsetai. So anepapha (untouchable) to those still bebēloi the hagia and hiera: 'tis koinōnia phōti pros skotos;' He apophaskei pantelōs (utterly forbids) making for themselves a like kataskeuē of oil. For idion monou tou Theou to hagiazein; as exaireton it anakeisetai (will be reserved) to him; to a genētē and pepoiēmenē physis how could hagiazein heterous be possible? It ploutei molis (is scarcely rich) ek metochēs tēs anōthen in hagiasmos. Fitting to epiboasthai to it with the saints' phōnē: 'ti echeis ho ouk elabes;' John of the Monogenēs: 'ek tou plērōmatos autou we all received'; and 'ouk ek metrou didōsi to Pneuma'; being rather pēgē hagiasmou he epimetrei (bestows/measures out) the Spirit to the axioi and hagiazei the logikē ktisis. 'Upon sarx anthrōpou it shall not be anointed,' though he prostetachōs (commanded) Aaron and the synierateuontes be anointed from it. So hyper anthrōpinon already the genos to hieron, as metochon of Christ ho hyper tēn ktisin. So anakomizōn (bringing up) us to the hyper physin axiōma, as it were apotemōn (cutting off) from the epigeia, tois anō prosnemei (assigns to those above): 'Patera,' he says, [cont. §31: 'mē kalesēte hymōn epi tēs gēs...'].
pass_a_gloss_with_greek: [cont. quotation] '[καλά]μου εὐώδους 250, and ἶρις (iris) 500 σίκλοι τοῦ ἁγίου, and ἔλαιον ἐξ ἐλαιῶν ἔσται; make it ἔλαιον χρῖσμα ἅγιον, μύρον μυρεψικόν (perfumer's ointment) τέχνῃ μυρεψοῦ; ἔλαιον χρῖσμα ἅγιον ἔσται. χρίσεις (anoint) with it the σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου, the κιβωτός and all its σκεύη, the λυχνία and its σκεύη, the θυσιαστήριον τοῦ θυμιάματος, the θυσιαστήριον τῶν ὁλοκαυτωμάτων and its σκεύη, the τράπεζα and its σκεύη, the λουτήρ and its βάσις; ἁγιάσεις them; they shall be Ἅγια τῶν ἁγίων; πᾶς ὁ ἁπτόμενος ἁγιασθήσεται. Aaron and his sons χρίσεις, ἁγιάσεις to ἱερατεύειν for me. To the sons of Israel: ἔλαιον ἄλειμμα χρίσεως ἅγιον for your γενεαί; ἐπὶ σάρκα ἀνθρώπου οὐ χρισθήσεται; κατὰ τὴν σύνθεσιν ταύτην you shall not make ὡσαύτως for yourselves; ἅγιον, ἁγίασμα to you. Whoever makes ὡσαύτως and gives of it to an ἀλλογενής ἐξολοθρευθήσεται from his λαός.' Of the ποιότης, σύνθεσις/συνθήκη, and ἀνισότης εἰς ὁλκήν (inequality of weight) of the εἴδη named, οὐδὲν ἂν ἔχοιμι φράσαι; φίλη the ἀλήθεια to those wont εὖ φρονεῖν. Ἔλαιον μύροις ἀνακραθέν (blended) would κατασημήνειεν the ἁγιασμός ἐν Χριστῷ διὰ Πνεύματος χορηγούμενος to the ἠλεημένοι; as 'ἐλίπανας (you anointed richly) ἐν ἐλαίῳ my head.' The σκηνή καταχρίεται and all in it; a τόπος also μετάσχοι ἁγιασμοῦ through the one ἐνοικῶν in it. The σκεύη ἁγιάζεται κατὰ τὸν πρέποντα τρόπον, as χρήσιμα for God's λειτουργίαι; ὁ ἁπτόμενος ἁγιασθήσεται. So ἀνέπαφα (untouchable) to those still βέβηλοι the ἅγια and ἱερά: 'τίς κοινωνία φωτὶ πρὸς σκότος;' He ἀποφάσκει παντελῶς (utterly forbids) making for themselves a like κατασκευή of oil. For ἴδιον μόνου τοῦ Θεοῦ τὸ ἁγιάζειν; as ἐξαίρετον it ἀνακείσεται (will be reserved) to him; to a γενητή and πεποιημένη φύσις how could ἁγιάζειν ἑτέρους be possible? It πλουτεῖ μόλις (is scarcely rich) ἐκ μετοχῆς τῆς ἄνωθεν in ἁγιασμός. Fitting to ἐπιβοᾶσθαι to it with the saints' φωνή: 'τί ἔχεις ὃ οὐκ ἔλαβες;' John of the Μονογενής: 'ἐκ τοῦ πληρώματος αὐτοῦ we all received'; and 'οὐκ ἐκ μέτρου δίδωσι τὸ Πνεῦμα'; being rather πηγή ἁγιασμοῦ he ἐπιμετρεῖ (bestows/measures out) the Spirit to the ἄξιοι and ἁγιάζει the λογικὴ κτίσις. 'Upon σάρξ ἀνθρώπου it shall not be anointed,' though he προστεταχώς (commanded) Aaron and the συνιερατεύοντες be anointed from it. So ὑπὲρ ἀνθρώπινον already the γένος τὸ ἱερόν, as μέτοχον of Christ ὁ ὑπὲρ τὴν κτίσιν. So ἀνακομίζων (bringing up) us to the ὑπὲρ φύσιν ἀξίωμα, as it were ἀποτεμών (cutting off) from the ἐπίγεια, τοῖς ἄνω προσνέμει (assigns to those above): 'Πατέρα,' he says, [cont. §31: 'μὴ καλέσητε ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς...'].
pass_b_english: Cyril: …calamus, two hundred and fifty; and of iris, five hundred shekels by the shekel of the sanctuary; and there shall be oil from olives. And you shall make of it a holy anointing oil, a perfumed ointment made by the perfumer’s art. It shall be a holy anointing oil. And with it you shall anoint the tent of witness, and the ark of the tent of witness and all its vessels, and the lampstand and all its vessels, and the altar of incense, and the altar of burnt offerings and all its vessels, and the table and all its vessels, and the laver and its base. And you shall sanctify them, and they shall be most holy. Whoever touches them shall be made holy. And you shall anoint Aaron and his sons, and sanctify them to serve me as priests. And you shall speak to the sons of Israel, saying: This shall be a holy anointing oil for you throughout your generations. Human flesh shall not be anointed with it, and you shall not make any like it for yourselves according to this composition. It is holy, and it shall be holy to you. Whoever makes any like it, and whoever gives any of it to a foreigner, shall be utterly destroyed from his people’ (Exodus 30:23–33). Now about the quality and the blending, and again about the unequal weights of the kinds named, I would have nothing to say; for truth is dear to those who are accustomed to think soundly. But oil blended with perfumes would signify, I think, the sanctification in Christ through the Spirit that is given to those who have received mercy, as in the words, ‘You anointed my head with oil’ (Psalm 23:5). The tent is anointed, and everything in it, for even a place may share in holiness through the one who dwells in it. The vessels too are sanctified, in the way that suits them, because they serve in the worship of God, and whoever touches them will be made holy (Exodus 30:29). So holy and sacred things may not be touched by those who are still profane; for, as it is written, ‘What fellowship has light with darkness?’ (2 Corinthians 6:14). And he absolutely forbids them to make a similar oil for themselves. For to sanctify belongs to God alone, and it will remain reserved to him as truly his own. How could a nature that has come into being and been made ever be able to sanctify others? For it is rich in holiness only with difficulty, through sharing in what comes from above. One might fittingly cry out to it in the words of the saints: ‘What do you have that you did not receive?’ (1 Corinthians 4:7). For John also says of the Only-begotten, ‘From his fullness we have all received’ (John 1:16), and, ‘He does not give the Spirit by measure’ (John 3:34); rather, being himself the fountain of holiness, he imparts the Spirit to the worthy and sanctifies the rational creation. ‘But human flesh,’ he says, ‘shall not be anointed with it’ (Exodus 30:32), although he had commanded that Aaron and those who serve as priests with him be anointed with it (Exodus 30:30). So the sacred race is already above the human, since it shares in Christ, who is above creation. That is why, raising us to a dignity beyond nature, and cutting us off, as it were, from earthly things, he assigns us to the things above. For he says,

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril De adoratione Book 9 exists. Translated fresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the earlier English of this book was not used as a base.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Boundary: §30 opens mid-word ('μου εὐώδους', completing καλά|μου from §29) inside the quotation of Exodus 30:22–33 LXX; the quotation's citation is placed at its close (Exodus 30:23–33), with 30:22–23 cited at its start in §29. The section ends with '«Πατέρα» γὰρ, φησί,'; chunk 8 opens §31 with the whole of Matthew 23:9 ('call no one on earth your father...'), which already carries 'Πατέρα', so §30 ends 'For he says,' to avoid doubling the word; the citation (Matthew 23:9) stands in §31. LXX details: ἶρις (iris) is the LXX rendering of Hebrew 'cassia' (Exodus 30:24); kept as 'iris'. 'σίκλους τοῦ ἁγίου' = 'by the shekel of the sanctuary'. Where the LXX of 30:24 has 'ἔλαιον ἐξ ἐλαιῶν ιν' (a hin of olive oil), Cyril's text reads 'ἔσται' ('there shall be oil from olives'), possibly a misreading of ιν; translated as printed. 'Ἅγια τῶν ἁγίων' (30:29) rendered 'most holy'. 'ἀλλογενεῖ' (30:33) = 'a foreigner'. LXX renumbering: Psalm 22:5 LXX = Psalm 23:5 English ('ἐλίπανας ἐν ἐλαίῳ τὴν κεφαλήν μου'). John 3:34 in John has God as giver; Cyril applies it to the Only-begotten as the source of holiness; translated as he uses it. 'ἐπιμετρεῖ' (measures out, bestows) rendered 'imparts', so that it does not seem to contradict 'not by measure'. 'τῆς τῶν ἁγίων φωνῆς' (the voice of the saints) introduces Paul's words in 1 Corinthians 4:7. 'πλουτεῖ μόλις ἐκ μετοχῆς τῆς ἄνωθεν' rendered 'it is barely rich in holiness itself, and only by sharing in what is from above'. 'τὸ γένος τὸ ἱερόν' (the sacred race, here the priestly people) may echo 1 Peter 2:9; not cited. Cyril admits he cannot explain the qualities, blend or weights of the spices; this is kept as an honest disclaimer, not smoothed away. Review: σκεύη rendered 'vessels' in the quotation, as in Cyril's comment and §27; ἁγιάσεις rendered 'sanctify' (not 'consecrate') so the quotation matches Cyril's argument that only God sanctifies.

changes: 'make it into oil, a holy anointing, a perfume blended' (stiff Greek order) -> 'make of it a holy anointing oil, a perfumed ointment made by the perfumer's art'
σκεύη 'utensils' -> 'vessels' (matches Cyril's comment); ἁγιάσεις 'consecrate' -> 'sanctify' (keeps the doctrinal link)
'holy oil of anointing' -> 'holy anointing oil'; 'I could say nothing' -> 'I would have nothing to say'
'barely rich in holiness itself, and only by sharing' -> 'rich in holiness only with difficulty, through sharing' (μόλις, no added 'only')
Refs checked: Exodus 30:23–33, 30:29, 30:30, 30:32 (LXX), Psalm 22:5 LXX = 23:5, 2 Corinthians 6:14, 1 Corinthians 4:7, John 1:16, 3:34
